svg.text: ANCIENT GREEK PROVERB · QUOTED BY PLATO
Each limb carries a craft; the centre holds the works.
Sixty days of work. Fly the middle path:
not so low the sea soaks the wings, not so high the sun melts the wax.
Dreams sent at night, as Oneiros came to Agamemnon
A year of work, swallowing its own tail.
WORKS IN ONE TURN OF THE SUN
